name: memory-authority-label
description: Use when you consolidate, summarize or rewrite memory (a MEMORY.md line, a topic file, a handoff, a compaction summary), and again when you are about to act on a remembered approval or instruction. Consolidation is an authorization boundary. It tends to keep a claim and drop the source constraints on its use, so the stored memory implies more authority than its source had. Record with each memory who said it, what kind of statement it was (standing instruction, one-time approval, user fact, observation, own inference, external content) and the scope it was given for, and at use time act only within that label. A remembered go-ahead is not a fresh confirmation. Distinct from memory-use-warrant (whether a memory may be surfaced) and cue-anchored-memory (how a fact gets delivered). Backed by AuthMem-Bench (arxiv 2608.01679). Triggers on consolidating memory and on acting on remembered authorization.
